name: Yearly budget and property tax rate

variants.name: Yearly budget and property tax rate (county and cities)
variants.summary: How a county or city sets its property tax rate and budget each year under the TRIM (Truth in Millage) law. The rate a body sends the Property Appraiser in July becomes, in practice, the highest rate it can adopt in September.
variants.dayCounting: TRIM periods count the later of July 1 or the value certification date as day 1 (s. 200.065(12), F.S.). Offsets here are calendar days added to the anchor date, so "within 35 days" is offset 0 to 34.

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for regular taxing authorities, Florida DOR

milestones.name: Budget calendar posted online
milestones.output: Public calendar of this year's budget steps

timing.rule: On or before January 30 each year.

residentCan.how: Use the calendar to put the workshop and hearing dates in your own calendar now.

milestones.influenceWhy: A schedule, not a decision, but it tells you when every later step happens.

milestones.name: Departments ask for money
milestones.output: Budget requests to the Manager or Mayor

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually winter or spring. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Tell your commissioner and the department head what service you want funded, before the request is written.
Ask for last year's department requests to see what was asked for and cut.

milestones.influenceWhy: Requests are still being written, but they are internal and not yet on any agenda.

milestones.name: Elected officials set budget priorities
milestones.output: Priorities the proposed budget must follow

timing.rule: Set by each body (a retreat, budget address or early workshop). Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Speak at the retreat or workshop if public comment is taken.
Send your commissioner one or two specific asks while priorities are open.

milestones.influenceWhy: Priorities steer the draft before numbers are fixed, but nothing is voted on yet.

milestones.name: Property Appraiser certifies taxable value
milestones.output: Certification of Taxable Value (Form DR-420) with the rolled-back rate

timing.rule: Assessment complete by July 1; this date (or a later certification date) is day 1 of the TRIM clock.

residentCan.how: Read the DR-420: it shows how much taxable value grew and the rolled-back rate (the rate that raises the same money as last year).

milestones.influenceWhy: A valuation by the Property Appraiser, not a policy choice by the body.

milestones.name: Mayor or Manager presents the proposed budget
milestones.output: Proposed budget and recommended tax rates

timing.rule: Set by the county charter and code or the city charter. County: the Mayor prepares it June 1 to July 15 and presents it no later than the day the Commission sets tentative rates.

residentCan.how: Read the proposed budget the day it is posted and note the lines you care about.
Ask your commissioner to raise a specific change before the rate cap vote.

milestones.influenceWhy: The draft now exists, so specific asks are possible, and the rate cap has not been voted yet.

milestones.name: Early budget workshops
milestones.output: Direction to staff before the rate cap is set

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually June or July. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend and speak if the workshop takes comment.
Email the commission before the workshop with a specific line item.

milestones.influenceWhy: Officials are still shaping the plan and can be moved before the July rate vote.

milestones.name: Commission sets the proposed (maximum) tax rate and first hearing date
milestones.output: Proposed millage, rolled-back rate and first hearing date sent to the Property Appraiser (DR-420)

timing.rule: Within 35 days of certification (day 35 is about August 4). A body that misses it cannot levy above the rolled-back rate.

residentCan.how: Speak at the July meeting where the proposed rate is voted.
Write to each commissioner before the vote asking for a specific rate, such as the rolled-back rate.
Call your district office the week of the vote.

milestones.influenceWhy: This rate goes on every TRIM notice and in practice caps the September rate; raising it later needs a new mailed notice to every taxpayer.

milestones.name: Budget workshops and town halls
milestones.output: Changes the commission asks for before the hearings

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually August. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend the town hall or workshop and ask about a specific line.
Email questions in advance so staff answer them in the room.

milestones.influenceWhy: Spending lines can still move, but the rate cap is already set.

milestones.name: TRIM notices mailed to property owners
inputs: Proposed rates and hearing dates from every taxing authority
milestones.output: Notice of Proposed Property Taxes (TRIM notice) to every owner

timing.rule: By the later of 55 days after certification (about August 24) or 10 days after the roll is approved.

residentCan.how: Check your notice: it lists each body's proposed rate and hearing date. To appeal your assessed value, petition the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the mailing (s. 194.011(3)(d), F.S.).
Use the hearing date on the notice to plan to speak.

milestones.influenceWhy: Turns the July rate into a dollar figure owners can see; strong turnout at the first hearing starts here.

milestones.name: Tentative budget posted online
milestones.output: Tentative budget on the official website

timing.rule: At least 5 days before the first budget hearing, and kept online at least 45 days.

residentCan.how: Download the tentative budget and compare it with the proposed one.

milestones.influenceWhy: Last look at the numbers before the hearing that fixes the ceiling.

milestones.name: First public budget hearing (tentative rate and budget)
milestones.output: Tentative millage and tentative budget adopted

timing.rule: Between day 65 and day 80 after certification (about September 3 to 18), after 5 p.m. on a weekday. The first item is the percent increase over the rolled-back rate. The county may not use a School Board hearing date; cities may not use county or School Board dates.

residentCan.how: Speak at the hearing: the public must be heard before any vote.
Send written comments before the hearing so they are in the record.

milestones.influenceWhy: The tentative rate set here is the most the final rate can be; the final hearing can only hold or lower it.

milestones.name: Final hearing advertised
milestones.output: Newspaper notice of the final hearing with a budget summary (Notice of Proposed Tax Increase if above rolled-back rate)

timing.rule: Within 15 days after the first hearing.

residentCan.how: Read the notice and send comments before the final hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: A notice, not a decision.

milestones.name: Final public budget hearing (final rate and budget)
milestones.output: Final millage and budget adopted, rate first, by separate votes

timing.rule: Not less than 2 nor more than 5 days after the ad first runs. The final rate may not exceed the tentative rate.

residentCan.how: Speak at the final hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The rate can still go down here, but not up, and most lines were settled at the first hearing.

milestones.name: Mayor may veto budget items
milestones.output: Veto message, or the budget stands

timing.rule: Within 10 days of final adoption. The Commission may override by two thirds of members present at its next regular meeting.

residentCan.how: Ask the Mayor's office to veto or keep a specific item within the 10 days.

milestones.influenceWhy: Rarely used and limited: vetoing revenue requires vetoing equal spending.

milestones.name: Adopted rate sent to Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
milestones.output: Rate on file for the November tax bills

timing.rule: Within 3 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the adopted millage resolution or ordinance.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork after the decision.

milestones.name: Fiscal year begins
milestones.output: Budget in effect October 1 to September 30

timing.rule: October 1.

residentCan.how: Watch for budget amendments during the year; they are adopted the same way as the budget.

milestones.influenceWhy: The budget is set; changes come only by amendment.

milestones.name: Certification of TRIM compliance to the state
milestones.output: Form DR-487 filed with the Florida Department of Revenue

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-487 package to check the ads and votes followed the law.

milestones.influenceWhy: A compliance filing; problems found here go to the Department of Revenue.

milestones.name: Final budget posted online
milestones.output: Adopted budget on the official website for at least 5 years

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Download the adopted budget to track spending during the year.

milestones.influenceWhy: Publication of a decision already made.

variants.name: Yearly school budget and property tax rate (school district)
variants.summary: School districts run on a faster TRIM clock: the tentative budget hearing is in late July, before TRIM notices go out. Most of the school tax rate is the required local effort set by the state; the board sets the discretionary rates.
variants.dayCounting: Same day counting as the regular TRIM template: the later of July 1 or certification is day 1 (s. 200.065(12), F.S.).

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for school districts, Florida DOR

milestones.name: Board budget workshops
milestones.output: Direction for the tentative budget

timing.rule: Set by the board, usually May and June. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend the workshop; ask the board to raise a specific priority.
Send written comments through the Citizen Information Center before the workshop.

milestones.influenceWhy: The last open stage before the tentative budget is drafted; the July ad and hearing then come within days.

milestones.name: Property Appraiser certifies school taxable value
milestones.output: Certification of School Taxable Value (Form DR-420S)

timing.rule: July 1 or the certification date, whichever is later, is day 1.

residentCan.how: Read the DR-420S to see the rolled-back rate.

milestones.influenceWhy: A valuation, not a board choice.

milestones.name: School fiscal year begins
milestones.output: District spends on ordinary expenses until the tentative budget becomes official

timing.rule: July 1. State law lets boards pay ordinary expenses from July 1 until the budget is official.

residentCan.how: Ask what the district is spending under the interim authority.

milestones.influenceWhy: Automatic.

milestones.name: State sets required local effort tax rate
inputs: Department of Revenue estimate of school taxable value
milestones.output: Required local effort millage certified to the board

timing.rule: Not later than July 19.

residentCan.how: This rate is set in Tallahassee; contact your state legislators about it, not the School Board.

milestones.influenceWhy: Set by the state; the board must levy it.

milestones.name: Superintendent submits the tentative budget
milestones.output: Tentative budget and proposed millage to the board

timing.rule: No later than 24 days after certification (about July 24).

residentCan.how: Read the tentative budget when it is posted with the July agenda.

milestones.influenceWhy: The draft exists; specific asks to board members can still change it before the hearing.

milestones.name: Tentative budget and tax rate advertised
milestones.output: Notice of the tentative budget hearing with a budget summary (Notice of Proposed Tax Increase if above rolled-back rate)

timing.rule: Within 29 days after certification (about July 29).

residentCan.how: Speak at the July regular meeting where the board authorizes the ad.

milestones.influenceWhy: The proposed rate becomes public here; the hearing follows within days.

milestones.name: Tentative budget posted online
milestones.output: Tentative budget on the district website

timing.rule: At least 2 days before the tentative budget hearing.

residentCan.how: Download it and bring specific questions to the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Last look before the hearing that sets the ceiling.

milestones.name: Tentative budget hearing
milestones.output: Tentative millage and budget adopted

timing.rule: Not less than 2 nor more than 5 days after the ad runs.

residentCan.how: Register to speak by the deadline for special meetings and speak at the hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Sets the tentative rate that goes on TRIM notices and caps the September rate.

milestones.name: Proposed rate sent to Property Appraiser
milestones.output: Proposed rate, rolled-back rate and final hearing date for the TRIM notice

timing.rule: Within 35 days of certification (about August 4).

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-420S as filed.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork carrying the July decision.

milestones.name: TRIM notices mailed
inputs: Proposed rates from every taxing authority
milestones.output: Notice of Proposed Property Taxes to every owner

timing.rule: By about 55 days after certification.

residentCan.how: Check the school line on your notice. Appeal your assessed value to the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of mailing (s. 194.011(3)(d), F.S.).

milestones.influenceWhy: Shows owners the school tax in dollars before the final hearing.

milestones.name: Final budget hearing
milestones.output: Final millage and budget adopted

timing.rule: Between day 65 and day 80 after certification (about September 3 to 18). No newspaper ad is required before it.

residentCan.how: Speak at the final hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The rate can be held or lowered here, not raised above the tentative rate.

milestones.name: Adopted rate sent to Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
milestones.output: Rate on file for tax bills

timing.rule: Within 3 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the adopted millage resolution.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork.

milestones.name: Certification of TRIM compliance to the state
milestones.output: Form DR-487 filed with the Department of Revenue

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for school districts, Florida DOR (DR-487)

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-487 package.

milestones.influenceWhy: Compliance filing.

milestones.name: Final budget posted online
milestones.output: Adopted budget on the district website

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Download the adopted budget.

milestones.influenceWhy: Publication of a decision already made.
